description: A modular, stack-agnostic toolkit for AI coding agents to autonomously find, reproduce, and patch vulnerabilities.

written.description: Reads a codebase and its commit history, builds a threat model from them, and sends agents to chase each hypothesis it raises. It then tries to reproduce each finding in a sandbox and attacks its own patch to check the fix holds, working from source alone with no running target.

alive.last_commit_message:
fix(core): node prompts are literal text, not ADK state templates

Found by the first evolved harness to reach a rollout: the domain proposer
quoted code in the threat modeler's prompt (f"... WHERE name='{name}'",
ORDER BY {column} {direction}) and the stage died before its first model
call with KeyError: "Context variable not found: `name`". ADK renders a
string instruction as a template -- {name} is a session-state lookup,
{artifact.x} an artifact load -- and a missing key is fatal at run time,
after validate_tree and the production loader have both passed the
workflow. Anyone hand-editing a prompt to include a code snippet hits the
same wall; the shipped prompts survive only because none of them contains
a bare {word}.

Mantis uses no state templating in node instructions (the seed prompt's
{filepath} is substituted by main.py itself), so every agent node now hands
its instruction to ADK as a provider, which ADK uses verbatim
(canonical_instruction returns bypass_state_injection=True).
LiteralInstruction is that provider and reads like the string it carries
(in, startswith, str, ==, len), so code that inspects an agent's prompt
keeps working.

Also in evals/evolve, from live attempts 6 and 7:
- the proposer's per-request timeout is 900 s (MANTIS_PROPOSER_LLM_TIMEOUT):
  a writing turn that emits several whole prompt files legitimately runs for
  minutes, and a 300 s cut was retried from zero and never completed; the
  session bound and the process kill guard against a dead connection;
- the proposer's output budget is 65k tokens clamped to the model's ceiling
  (MANTIS_PROPOSER_MAX_OUTPUT_TOKENS): the investigation proposer's writing
  turn hit the provider default (FinishReason.MAX_TOKENS) twice, losing
  every edit in it; the instructions now also say one file per call, at
  most two per turn.

Tests: tests/test_literal_instruction.py reproduces the KeyError through
ADK's inject_session_state on the string form and shows the provider form
bypasses it, checks every shipped node carries one, and loads an evolved
prompt with braces verbatim; tests/test_evolve.py covers the timeout floor
and the output clamp.

Change-Id: I4f067259b9d72c9eaf81e0a902c28d8e380491d0
